claims.quote: Other than in the anal canal, the mucosa of the colon is simple columnar epithelium made mostly of enterocytes (absorptive cells) and goblet cells.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.quote: An epithelial cell that has its apical plasma membrane folded into microvilli to provide ample surface for the absorption of nutrients from the intestinal lumen.
The micelles move into the brush border of the small intestine absorptive cells

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: brush border enzymes (digestive enzymes set in the microvillus membrane)
claims.quote: The small intestine’s absorptive cells also synthesize digestive enzymes and then place them in the plasma membranes of the microvilli.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.quote: The long-chain fatty acids and monoglycerides recombine in the absorptive cells to form triglycerides, which aggregate into globules and become coated with proteins. These large spheres are called chylomicrons.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Its apical membrane is folded into microvilli, which gives it a large surface for absorbing nutrients from the intestinal lumen.
claims.quote: An epithelial cell that has its apical plasma membrane folded into microvilli to provide ample surface for the absorption of nutrients from the intestinal lumen.

claims.value: It passes absorbed fat on as chylomicrons, which it releases by exocytosis into the lacteals of the villi.
claims.quote: Chylomicrons leave the enterocytes by exocytosis and enter the lymphatic system via lacteals in the villi of the intestine.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
